entry.evidence: Even with large GPS data sets, detecting SSEs is still challenging in Boso Peninsular

sequences.source_document: Published paper PDF and publisher XML text

steps.action: Boso SSEs are taken as an established, quasi-periodic phenomenon from earlier studies, with recurrence intervals shortened after 2011.
steps.quote: This tectonic setting in the region has led to periodical SSEs recorded since the 1990s.

steps.action: The authors pose the aim: recover the detailed spatio-temporal slip history of the post-2011 Boso SSEs from GPS using PCAIM.
steps.quote: Therefore, we aim to employ this PCAIM to recover the spatio-temporal evolution of SSEs offshore the Boso Peninsula.

steps.action: Daily coordinates from 77 GEONET stations, 2009-2019, processed by the Nevada Geodetic Laboratory with GIPSY/OASIS-II, are assembled.
steps.quote: We use the daily GPS data from 77 GPS stations of the GPS Earth Observation Network System (GEONET)

steps.action: The inversion is designed: a rectangular plate-interface fault from Nishimura (Table 1) is discretized into 20 x 25 triangular patches of about 6 km, with the smoothing factor set by chi-square and a slab model from ERI.
steps.quote: We approximate the geometry of the plate interface with a rectangular fault

steps.action: Best-fit chi-square values (12.4, 13.5, 11.7) are compared with Nishimura's 14.8 to argue that the resolution and smoothing factor are acceptable.
steps.quote: In Nishimura's inversion for a slip deficit rate in the Tokyo region, the chi-square value of the best-fitting model is 14.8 [35]

steps.action: A new time-series processing tool fits a trajectory model (Eq. 1): steps, velocity from 2009-2011, logarithmic Tohoku relaxation, and seasonal terms with order set by ABIC and estimated from non-SSE years. The residuals are taken as the SSE signal.
steps.quote: we develop a new GPS coordinate time series processing software to obtain these SSE-induced deformations from high-noise GPS data

steps.action: The logarithmic relaxation-time behaviour (Gaussian, distance-dependent, close to 1 in Boso) is taken from the authors' earlier study [39].
steps.quote: is significantly related to the epicenter distance, and obeys the Gaussian distribution [39]

steps.action: Residual E/N/U series (e.g. J266, Fig. 4) show three transients, in 2011, 2013-2014 and 2018. The March 2011 hidden SSE is set aside.
steps.quote: Three SSEs can be observed in three durations

steps.action: PCAIM (centering, SVD, Okada Green functions, depth limited to 30 km, horizontal:vertical weights 5:1) is applied to the extracted series of the 77 stations in three test windows to estimate slip distributions.
steps.quote: we use the PCAIM to resolve the slip distribution of SSEs

steps.action: Common-mode error is evaluated by stacking distant sites (Fig. 5) and by PCA. A one-component solution is compared with a two-component one (Fig. 6): chi-square changes by no more than 0.1, so one component is kept.
steps.quote: subtracting the CMEs isolated by the stacking or PCA methods has little effect on Boso SSEs inversion

steps.action: Extracted and PCAIM-computed displacements are compared at stations and network-wide (Figs. 7, 8). The south-eastward motion, opposite to Philippine Sea plate motion, is read as slip on the plate interface.
steps.quote: the extracted and computed horizontal displacements are consistent overall

steps.action: The displacement time series are compared with Ozawa's ENIF estimates.
steps.quote: our results are in good agreement with the estimated displacement time series from Ozawa using the ENIF software [30]

steps.action: Cumulative slip, its uncertainty, moment release and durations are derived (Figs. 9, 10, Table 2): maximum slip 12.4, 4.8 and 9.2 cm; Mw 6.7, 6.4 and 6.6. The 2013-2014 slip is about 5 km deeper.
steps.quote: The maximum cumulative slip is the slow slip of the 2018 SSE, which can reach 12.4 cm

steps.action: Slip amplitude, depth and magnitude are compared with Ozawa (larger slip, shallower), Fukuda (consistent location) and Gardonio (Mw 6.4-6.6).
steps.quote: Compared to Ozawa's studies [30], the cumulative slips of three SSEs are generally more minor

steps.action: Slip evolution is estimated in 2-day steps (Figs. 11-13): onset, acceleration and deceleration, maximum slip rates of 2.1, 1.3 and 1.8 cm/day, slip-zone expansion and shrinkage, and two phases in 2011.
steps.quote: we recognize that the 2018 SSE began on June 6, 2018, offshore eastern side of the Boso Peninsula

steps.action: The 2013-2014 maximum slip rate (1.3 cm/day) is compared with Ozawa's ENIF value (1.1 cm/day), and the migration pattern with Fukuda's.
steps.quote: calculated by Ozawa using ENIF [30]

steps.action: The claim is kept that the three SSEs differ in nucleation style, with 2011 the most complex (two phases) and 2013-2014 the fastest.
steps.quote: the nucleation of the 2011 SSE is the most complex involving two processes

steps.action: In the Discussion, durations are compared with earlier Boso SSE studies, and differences from the ENIF results (smaller slip, about 5 km deeper) are noted while trends are judged consistent.
steps.quote: the spatio-temporal variation trends of the three SSEs are almost relatively consistent

steps.action: The 2011-2019 recurrence (2.2-4 yr) is compared with the cited pre-2011 regularity of 4-7 yr.
steps.quote: our study shows that the recurrence interval has changed from 2.2 to 4 years from 2011 to 2019

steps.action: The shortening is attributed to the Tohoku earthquake, using numerical friction-model results from Gardonio et al.
steps.quote: Numerical friction models indicate that the recurrence interval of SSEs may be shortened when a large inter-plate earthquake is about to occur nearby [34].

steps.action: The regularity is extended to a conditional expectation that the next SSE comes 4-7 years after 2018 if no large earthquake intervenes.
steps.quote: According to the periodicity of Boso SSEs

end.claim: Three Boso SSEs (2011, 2013-2014, 2018) are detected in post-Tohoku GPS residuals. PCAIM gives their slip histories (Mw 6.6, 6.4, 6.7; maximum slip 9.2, 4.8, 12.4 cm), which reveal different nucleation styles.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the PCAIM inversion of the extracted SSE series onto the Okada fault model, there would be no slip distributions, moments or spatio-temporal evolution, which form the paper's claim.

gates.evidence: The data are archived GEONET solutions not collected for a hypothesis. The claim faced only a fit check (extracted versus computed displacements) and qualitative comparisons with published ENIF and other estimates; mismatches (smaller slip, 5 km deeper) were attributed to method differences rather than counted against the claim. Nothing was fixed in advance: the smoothing factor and component number were chosen by chi-square after the data were seen.

limits:
Location convention: the supplied XML holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps cite printed journal pages and quote the PDF text.

Composition: none_fits is coded because the walk is method building, then observation of found events, then latent-slip estimation, with no stated rivals. It is not a trace series (no rival explanations) and not capability_first (the phenomenon was already established). The nearest is natures_repetition, through the recurrence discussion.

What the paper does not show:
- No synthetic resolution test (checkerboard or recovery test) of the 6 km fault model; the sub-mm PCAIM uncertainties are formal only.
- No variation of the post-seismic (logarithmic) model, though separating afterslip from SSEs is named as the main difficulty.
- The comparisons with Ozawa, Fukuda and Gardonio are qualitative comparisons with published numbers, not reanalyses.
- The reviewers are acknowledged, but no review file is supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

Sub-claims and their status:
- The differing nucleation styles are an interpretation of the inversion: best_explanation at most, with no rivals.
- The recurrence shortening attributed to Tohoku rests on cited friction models: best_explanation.
- The 4-7 yr expectation for the next SSE is an untested conditional extrapolation: claim_status none.

Inconsistencies in the paper:
- The conclusion calls the fault model a 'point source model', whereas Section 2.2 describes triangular patches on a rectangular fault.
- Reference [18] is an unrelated polymer-micelle paper, and [13] and [21] duplicate each other. Inference: there are citation errors.

disagreements.support: The PCAIM cumulative slips, moments and maximum slip rates are smaller than Ozawa's, and the slip lies about 5 km deeper. The authors attribute this to different extraction or inversion methods without testing it.

disagreements.target: Ozawa et al. 2019 [30] (depth of the 2018 SSE)
disagreements.support: The slip centre agrees with Fukuda for 2013-2014 but is 5 km deeper than Ozawa's 2018 solution; only the inversion results are offered as evidence.
disagreements.quote: but 5 km deeper than that of Ozawa's studies on 2018 SSE [30]
